data.title: Sort
data.tagline: Sorting puts a list in order by one field—newest first, or largest amount first—without removing a single record.
data.learningOutcome: You can turn "I want X on top" into "sort by field ascending/descending," and tell sorting from filtering.
data.description: A quote list can default to newest first, and tapping the amount header flips to largest first. Sorting and filtering partner in opposite directions: filtering hides non-matching records and shortens the list, while sorting keeps every record and only reorders. Telling an AI "sort by creation time descending" beats "put the new ones on top."

learning.assumes: You have sorted photos by time or clicked a table column header.
learning.outcome: You can turn "I want X on top" into "sort by field ascending/descending," and tell sorting from filtering.

distinctions.label: Filter
distinctions.explanation: Filter hides non-matching records and shortens the list; Sort reorders records without losing any.

distinctions.label: Search
distinctions.explanation: Search finds records matching keywords; Sort arranges the found records by a field.

explanation.title: Ascending and descending
explanation.text: Ascending goes small to large (1, 2, 3); descending goes large to small (3, 2, 1). "Newest on top" is creation time descending.

explanation.title: State the default sort
explanation.text: The order on open is the default sort. Specifying "newest by creation time" keeps the AI from picking an arbitrary alphabetical order.

data.boundary: Sorting is not filtering: filtering narrows the list, sorting reorders it without losing a record—they often combine, filtering "following up" then sorting by amount. Pinning a row to the top is also not sorting; it manually pins one record and leaves the rest untouched.

lessonPractice.title: To see "the largest quotes," which operation does NOT reduce the number of records in the list?

options.label: Sort by amount, largest first
options.feedback: Correct. Sorting only reorders—every record stays, the largest ones move to the top.

options.label: Filter to records above 10,000
options.feedback: Filtering hides non-matching records and shortens the list—the count changes. That is filtering, not sorting.

options.label: Delete the small-amount records
options.feedback: Deleting removes the data itself. Viewing order should never be built on deletion.

data.agentPrompt: Make the amount column clickable to toggle largest-first and smallest-first, leaving other columns alone. After the change, I will tap the amount header on mobile to confirm the order changes while the record count stays the same.
